title: Guard site-docs section renames with legacy aliases and a no-silent-drop test
goal:
# Guard site-docs section renames with legacy aliases and a no-silent-drop test

## Context
Case study: KainBain task 68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393 (docs viewer sidebar regroup, from how-it-works/working-with to four new section ids). The upgrade-safety audit (docs/tasks/68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393/continueity-failure-20261115-214114.md) reproduced live that api/siteDocs.js readDocFile returned null for old section values, so listDocs returned [] and getDoc returned null on a custom KAINBAIN_SITE_DOCS dir using old frontmatter: custom articles silently vanish on update with no alias, warning, or DEPRECATIONS.md entry. The branch fixed it ad hoc with LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES plus a deprecation note, but no automated guardrail stops the next rename from repeating the silent drop. All existing API suites passed with the new sections, so tests alone did not catch it.

## Steps
1. Add a permanent regression test proving listDocs/getDoc on a custom docs dir using retired section ids still resolves (via alias or explicit warn), never silently [].
2. Add a rename guardrail for DOC_SECTIONS in api/siteDocs.js: removing or renaming a section id without a LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES entry (or equivalent documented mapping) fails a cheap check with a message naming the retired id.
3. Document the required rename procedure (alias plus DEPRECATIONS.md entry) where the taxonomy is defined so future agents follow it first time.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A section rename without an alias entry fails the new check, naming the retired id.
- [ ] Old-section frontmatter still indexes (aliased) with a recorded warning, covered by a regression test.
- [ ] Valid renames with alias plus deprecation note pass.

## Notes
Structural follow-on from task 68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393; see its continuity-failure report and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md for the full case study. No existing open ticket covers this (checked: binary-safe proof ticket b1c069e0 and flaky-CI quarantine ticket 8769b002 are completed and address different failure modes).

# Guard site-docs section renames with legacy aliases and a no-silent-drop test

## Context
Case study: KainBain task 68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393 (docs viewer sidebar regroup, from how-it-works/working-with to four new section ids). The upgrade-safety audit (docs/tasks/68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393/continueity-failure-20261115-214114.md) reproduced live that api/siteDocs.js readDocFile returned null for old section values, so listDocs returned [] and getDoc returned null on a custom KAINBAIN_SITE_DOCS dir using old frontmatter: custom articles silently vanish on update with no alias, warning, or DEPRECATIONS.md entry. The branch fixed it ad hoc with LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES plus a deprecation note, but no automated guardrail stops the next rename from repeating the silent drop. All existing API suites passed with the new sections, so tests alone did not catch it.

## Steps
1. Add a permanent regression test proving listDocs/getDoc on a custom docs dir using retired section ids still resolves (via alias or explicit warn), never silently [].
2. Add a rename guardrail for DOC_SECTIONS in api/siteDocs.js: removing or renaming a section id without a LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES entry (or equivalent documented mapping) fails a cheap check with a message naming the retired id.
3. Document the required rename procedure (alias plus DEPRECATIONS.md entry) where the taxonomy is defined so future agents follow it first time.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A section rename without an alias entry fails the new check, naming the retired id.
- [ ] Old-section frontmatter still indexes (aliased) with a recorded warning, covered by a regression test.
- [ ] Valid renames with alias plus deprecation note pass.

## Notes
Structural follow-on from task 68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393; see its continuity-failure report and IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md for the full case study. No existing open ticket covers this (checked: binary-safe proof ticket b1c069e0 and flaky-CI quarantine ticket 8769b002 are completed and address different failure modes).

52|  warning naming the id and the fix — the old silent shape is gone.

The branch fixed that instance ad hoc; this task builds the permanent guardrail, since all existing API suites passed with the new sections and did not catch the break.
6|
7|## 2. Guiding principle — make the change easy, then make the change
8|
9|Phases 0–A change no guardrail behavior: they pin down the decisions (survey defaults), centralize the taxonomy history in one asserted place, and add shared test fixtures for legacy frontmatter dirs. Phase B then lands the regression test, the rename guardrail, and the documented procedure as small edits on those seams. Phase C proves the guardrail both ways (red without alias, green with alias) and runs the full gates. Do not start Phase B until the Phase 0 decisions are confirmed and Phase A fixtures are green.
10|
11|## 3. Current-state facts (researched this run)
12|
13|- Taxonomy source of truth: `api/siteDocs.js` — `DOC_SECTIONS` (line 35: `["getting-started", "concepts", "workflows", "reference"]`), `SECTION_LABELS`, `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` (`how-it-works → concepts`, `working-with → workflows`), and `readDocFile` (lines 133–166), which resolves aliases with a `console.warn` naming the file, then returns `null` for still-unknown sections.
14|- Ad-hoc fix already landed: [DEPRECATIONS.md](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175/DEPRECATIONS.md) has a "Docs taxonomy rename" section (2026-11-15) stating the alias is retained indefinitely, and [api/siteDocs.test.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175/api/siteDocs.test.js) has a `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` suite (3 tests: mapping equality, `readDocFile` resolves old sections, `listDocs`/`getDoc` index old-section custom articles). Gap: no test asserts the warning is emitted, and nothing fails if a *future* rename drops an id without adding an alias.
15|- Frontend mirror: [frontend/src/components/docs/docsSections.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175/frontend/src/components/docs/docsSections.js) duplicates order/labels; [api/siteDocs.frontendParity.test.js](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175/api/siteDocs.frontendParity.test.js) locks the two copies together. 19|## 4. Survey decisions (from SURVEY.md)
20|
21|[SURVEY.md](/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175/docs/tasks/ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175/SURVEY.md) asked three questions; no answers were recorded in the file, so this plan adopts the marked Recommended option for each as the decided default (confirm in Phase 0; each is reversible before Phase B):
22|
23|| # | Question | Adopted decision (Recommended) | Plan consequence |
24||---|----------|-------------------------------|------------------|
25|| q1 | What happens to old-category articles? | Show under the new name automatically + record a warning for the site owner | Keep alias resolution + `console.warn`; regression test asserts both; no reader-facing "moved" notice |
26|| q2 | How long do old names keep working? | Forever | Aliases are never removed; guardrail asserts the known-history set only grows; matches the existing "retained indefinitely" note |

29|If the implementer hears otherwise from the task owner, only q1/q2 change behavior (warn text, alias lifetime); the guardrail shape in Phase B is unchanged.
30|
31|## 5. Key decisions
32|
33|1. **Guardrail mechanism: a committed vitest history assertion, not a new script.** A test in `api/` (extended `siteDocs.test.js` or a small new `siteDocs.taxonomy.test.js`) holds a `KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY` list of every section id ever shipped. Rejected alternative: a standalone `scripts/check-*` job — heavier, needs new CI wiring, and the parity/integrity tests prove `vitest` is the established home for taxonomy guards.
34|2. **Alias-target and deprecation-note coupling included in the same check.** The guardrail also asserts every alias target is a current `DOC_SECTIONS` member (catches dangling aliases after a second rename) and that `DEPRECATIONS.md` mentions each retired id (catches alias-without-note). Reading `DEPRECATIONS.md` from the test follows the integrity-test precedent; message names the missing piece.
35|3. **Warning stays owner-facing `console.warn`, and the regression test asserts it.** Survey q1's recommended option is exactly current behavior; the gap is only that no test locks it. Use `vi.spyOn(console, "warn")` around `readDocFile`/`listDocs` on a legacy dir and assert the retired id and filename appear. Rejected: reader-facing "moved" banner (survey non-recommended) and silent aliasing (repeats the original failure mode).
36|4. **Procedure documented where the taxonomy is defined.** The required rename checklist (alias + warn + `DEPRECATIONS.md` entry + history-list update + test run) lives in the `DOC_SECTIONS` docblock in `api/siteDocs.js` as the primary copy future agents read first, with a one-line pointer from `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` and no second full copy elsewhere (avoids drift).
37|
38|## 6. Step-by-step work plan
39|
40|### PHASE 0 — Grounding and decisions first (no code change; biggest unknowns up front)
41|
42|**Step 1 — Confirm survey defaults and guardrail home.**
43|Confirm the three adopted survey defaults (§4) with the task owner (or record them as assumed if unreachable), and confirm the guardrail lives as a vitest history assertion in `api/` per Key Decision 1. Output: a short decision note appended to this plan's task folder if anything deviates from §4–§5.
44|*Why first:* q1/q2 answers change the warn/lifetime contract; settling them before fixtures avoids rewriting tests.
45|
46|**Step 2 — Reproduce the original silent drop against current HEAD (red-team baseline).**
47|In a scratch temp dir (never committed), write two `.md` files with old `how-it-works`/`working-with` frontmatter, then run a throwaway node/vitest probe asserting `listDocs`/`getDoc` resolve them today (proves the ad-hoc alias works), and a second probe with the alias temporarily stubbed out proving `listDocs` returns `[]` / `getDoc` returns `null` (reproduces the continuity-failure report). Keep the probes in `/tmp`, not the repo.
48|*Why first:* this is the "big research piece" — it re-verifies the case study on the current tree and defines the exact red/green boundary the guardrail must enforce.
49|
50|### PHASE A — Make the change easy (seams + fixtures, no behavior change)
51|
52|**Step 3 — Add a shared legacy-docs-dir fixture helper for tests.**
53|Add a tiny helper (co-located with the siteDocs tests) such as `writeLegacyDocsDir(files)` that creates a temp dir of articles with given `section:` frontmatter and returns its path. Refactor the existing `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` suite's inline temp-dir setup onto it with zero assertion changes; suite stays green.
54|*Why first:* the new regression + guardrail tests both need legacy dirs; one helper keeps them small and consistent.
55|
56|**Step 4 — Introduce the `KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY` seam (asserted, initially passing).**
57|Add the history list (initial value: the four current ids plus `how-it-works` and `working-with`) either as a test-local constant or an export from `api/siteDocs.js` next to `DOC_SECTIONS`, plus a passing assertion of the history ⊆ (current ∪ aliased) invariant. No failure-message polish yet; just the seam and a green test.
58|*Why first:* the guardrail in Phase B becomes a message + coupling upgrade on this seam rather than new machinery.
59|
60|### PHASE B — The change (small edits on the seams)
61|
62|**Step 5 — Harden the no-silent-drop regression test (acceptance criterion 2).**
63|Extend the legacy suite: (a) `listDocs` on a legacy-only dir is non-empty and maps to the aliased sections; (b) `getDoc` resolves each legacy slug (never `null`); (c) `console.warn` was called once per aliased file and the message names the retired id and filename. Cover both retired ids. This is the permanent proof old-section frontmatter still indexes via alias with a recorded warning.
64|
65|**Step 6 — Build the rename guardrail (acceptance criteria 1 and 3).**
66|Upgrade the Phase A assertion into the full guardrail: for every id in `KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY`, fail naming the retired id when it is neither current nor aliased; fail naming the alias when a target is not current; fail naming the retired id when `DEPRECATIONS.md` does not mention it. Each failure message states the exact fix (add the alias entry, correct the target, add the deprecation note) and points to the `DOC_SECTIONS` docblock procedure. Mutation-check immediately (see Step 8).
67|
68|**Step 7 — Document the rename procedure at the taxonomy definition.**
69|Write the required checklist into the `DOC_SECTIONS` docblock in `api/siteDocs.js`: (1) choose the new id and update `DOC_SECTIONS`/`SECTION_LABELS` (+ frontend mirror, locked by the parity test); (2) add `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES['<old>'] = '<new>'` (never delete entries — aliases are forever per survey q2); (3) add a `DEPRECATIONS.md` entry (retired id, new id, date, auto-migration note); (4) append the retired id to `KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY` if it is not already there; (5) migrate in-repo `site-docs/*.md` frontmatter; (6) run the siteDocs suites. Add a one-line pointer from the `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` docblock. Keep it concise — a checklist, not an essay — so future agents follow it first time.
70|
71|### PHASE C — Assurance (prove it both ways, then run the gates)
72|
73|**Step 8 — Mutation probes: red without alias, green with alias (the highest-risk validation).**
74|With throwaway local edits (reverted immediately, or via `git stash`): (a) remove one `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` entry → the guardrail test fails naming that retired id; (b) rename a `DOC_SECTIONS` id without adding an alias → the guardrail test fails naming the retired id; (c) perform a valid rename (new id + alias + `DEPRECATIONS.md` mention + history update) → the full siteDocs suites pass. Record the exact failure messages in the task notes as proof each acceptance criterion is enforced, not just asserted.
75|
76|**Step 9 — Full automated verification.**
77|Run `npm run test:api` (all siteDocs suites incl. new guardrail, parity, integrity, deploy-layout), `npm run lint:api`, and root `npm run docs:check` (doc-link + jsdoc-example checks cover the edited docblocks). All green required; no frontend or visual suites affected (no UI change).
78|
79|**Step 10 — Task documentation.**
80|Record in the task folder: the survey-default confirmation (Step 1), the red-team baseline result (Step 2), and the mutation-probe failure messages (Step 8). No `site-docs/` article changes needed (this is contributor-facing procedure, not user docs); the `DEPRECATIONS.md` taxonomy section needs no edit unless Step 8's valid-rename probe used a real id (it must not — use a fake id and revert).
81|
82|## 7. Validation plan (maps to acceptance criteria)
83|
84|| Acceptance criterion | Validation | Expected evidence |
85||----------------------|------------|-------------------|
86|| Rename without alias fails the new check, naming the retired id | Step 8 probes (a) and (b) | Guardrail test output containing the retired id (e.g. `working-with`) plus the fix pointer; recorded in task notes |
87|| Old-section frontmatter still indexes (aliased) with a recorded warning, covered by a regression test | Step 5 suite + `npm run test:api` | New/extended tests green; `listDocs` non-empty, `getDoc` non-null, `console.warn` asserted per file |
88|| Valid renames with alias plus deprecation note pass | Step 8 probe (c) + Step 9 | Full `test:api` + `lint:api` + `docs:check` green on a valid-rename tree |
89|
90|## 8. Risks and mitigations
91|
92|- **Over-coupling the test to `DEPRECATIONS.md` prose:** assert only that each retired id string appears in the file, not its wording — robust to copy edits, still catches a missing entry.
93|- **History list itself drifting:** the guardrail fails closed — an id in neither current sections nor aliases fails with the id named, so forgetting the history update surfaces as the same loud failure, not silence.
94|- **Double-alias chains after a second rename:** alias targets must be current ids (Key Decision 2), so a rename of an already-aliased target fails until both entries point at the live id; document this in the checklist.
95|- **Frontend mirror drift on a real rename:** out of scope for the guardrail itself — already covered by `siteDocs.frontendParity.test.js`; the checklist references it.
96|- **Survey had no recorded answers:** mitigated by adopting Recommended defaults explicitly in §4 and confirming in Step 1 before any test is written.
97|
98|## 9. Non-goals
99|
100|- No generic rename-protection framework for other taxonomies (survey q3: docs categories only).
101|- No reader-facing "moved" notices (survey q1: owner-facing warning only).
102|- No alias expiry or removal schedule (survey q2: forever; matches "retained indefinitely").
103|- No frontend, sidebar, or styling changes; no new dependencies or CI jobs.
104|
105|## 10. Definition of done
106|
107|A section rename without an alias entry fails the new check naming the retired id; old-section frontmatter still indexes (aliased) with a recorded warning, covered by a regression test; valid renames with alias plus deprecation note pass; the rename procedure is documented in the `DOC_SECTIONS` docblock; `test:api`, `lint:api`, and `docs:check` are green; mutation-probe evidence is recorded in the task folder.

## Ticket 1 — Fix rename-procedure step 4 so it cannot duplicate history entries

Title: `Fix siteDocs rename procedure step 4 to prevent history duplication`

to `KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY`". That instruction is literally wrong: the
taxonomy guardrail requires every current section id to already be listed

the entry and fails the hygiene assertion (`lists "x" twice — keep one
entry`). Reword the step to "ensure the retired id is listed (append only
if missing) and append the brand-new id". Then prove both directions: (a)
a scratch rename following the new wording passes `npm run test --prefix
api -- siteDocs` and `npm run docs:check` with no hygiene failure;

## Ticket 2 — Derive the site-docs taxonomy bottom-up so renames stop touching N files

Title: `Derive site-docs taxonomy from content to shrink rename touch-points`

Goal (standalone): Today a site-docs section rename must touch
`DOC_SECTIONS`, `SECTION_LABELS`, `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES`,
`KNOWN_SECTION_HISTORY`, `DEPRECATIONS.md`, the frontend
`docsSections.js` mirror, and several exact-equality test assertions
(proven by the valid-rename mutation probe, which needed all of these for
a green run). Every touch-point is a place a future agent can miss and a
reason renames take multiple iterations. Reduce this structurally,
honouring the owner's stated direction ("docs derived … bottom up so we
don't have to maintain a central list"): investigate deriving section
ids/labels from the shipped `site-docs/` content (and/or consolidating
the frontend mirror and pinned test lists onto the single
`api/siteDocs.js` source of truth) so a rename touches the minimum
possible set of files. Hard constraints that must keep passing: retired
ids keep resolving via `LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES` with an owner-facing
warning (never a silent drop), the taxonomy guardrail still fails loudly
naming any retired id without an alias, and the full `test:api`,
`lint:api`, `docs:check` gates stay green. Deliverable is the smallest
structural change that removes at least one manual touch-point (or a
written finding, with evidence, that derivation is unsafe — e.g. custom
`KAINBAIN_SITE_DOCS` dirs needing ids absent from shipped content — plus
the next-cheapest consolidation instead). Context (optional): case
studies `68714709-3f50-4e5c-bfa6-bac16a36c393` (silent doc drop on
sidebar regroup) and `ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175`
(section-rename guardrail); owner direction in
`docs/tasks/ee3ca5d2-8b05-4908-bbd1-808c667d1175/SURVEY.md` q2 note.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] A section rename requires strictly fewer manual file edits than
        today, with the removed touch-point(s) named in the task notes.
